title: SemiVL: Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation with Vision-Language Guidance
mechanism: Spatially fine-tuned CLIP, a language-guided decoder, and class definitions given as text to separate confusable classes, inside UniMatch-style SSL.
adaptation: Write text definitions for gridline, splice, edge_dark, material and crack in EL terms. CLIP has little EL prior and ViT-B/16 at 512 px is coarse, so the use is mainly as a benchmark SSL baseline and a test for the weak structural classes.
min_experiment: Run the official code on our split as a benchmark arm vs UniMatch V2 and house PF, 3 seeds. Metric: mIoU_rob, gridline IoU, splice IoU. Kill as a candidate model if mIoU_rob is below house PF.
evidence: R: +13.5 mIoU on COCO with 232 labels and +6.1 on VOC with 92 labels over the prior SOTA; gains are at scarce labels.
prior_overlap: Vision-language models were never tried. Open, but the evidence is low-label only.
